sections.html:
North central Alabama is home to Cullman County, where the city of Cullman is both the seat and the largest city. The county grew 9.3 percent from 80,406 residents in 2010 to 87,866 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 94,009 adds another 7.0 percent. The 2020 count found 34,723 households in 39,145 housing units, of which 11.3 percent were vacant. Owners occupy 74.2 percent of occupied homes, rental vacancy is 6.4 percent, and 75.6 percent of residents live outside urban areas.

With a median age of 41.3, many sellers are long-time owners sitting on decades of equity. Rentals tend to fill, since the rental vacancy rate is low. Most houses are reached by county roads, and the county school system covers unincorporated areas and nearly every municipality. Arab and Cullman run their own systems, so the district depends on the address, and buyers will ask.

The 2011 tornado on April 27 of that year left repairs behind in parts of the county. Expect an inspector to ask about storm repair history on older houses.

sections.h2: Cities, towns and what the lines mean for a sale
sections.html:
There are four cities: Arab (mostly in Marshall County), Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville. The nine towns are Baileyton, Berlin, Colony, Dodge City, Fairview, Garden City (partly in Blount County), Holly Pond, South Vinemont and West Point. East Point and Joppa are census-designated places, and Joppa is partly in Marshall County. Beyond these, the county has more than twenty named unincorporated communities, among them Arkadelphia, Bremen, Crane Hill, Logan, Simcoe, Vinemont and Welti.

Many sellers live in one of those communities and not in a city. Confirm which taxing bodies and which school system apply to your parcel before you talk price.

Alcohol rules follow the city line. Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville allow sales, and the rest of the county is dry. If you own a building that a restaurant or shop might want, the parcel's side of that line affects who can use it.

sections.h2: Due dates and the delinquency timetable
sections.html:
Bills are payable starting October 1, and a balance left past December 31 is delinquent.

MonthStep for an unpaid account
October 1Tax due
January 1Tax delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to the probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

Courtesy notices are all you can expect from the Revenue Commissioner, so a missing statement is no defense. To dispute a value, file a written protest with the Board of Equalization inside 30 days of your valuation notice. Anyone 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or blind owes no state portion once the exemption is claimed.

January and February are tricky for sellers. A sale closing then may still have last year's bill open, and the closing agent is trained to catch it.

Alabama counties work through one quarter of their parcels annually, which means a full pass takes four years. Buildings discovered in a review go on the rolls for the following tax year. The purpose is to prevent sharp jumps in value and keep revenue steady for schools, cities, counties and the state. To learn when your neighborhood comes up, phone the Revenue Commissioner.

Report new improvements or removals by December 31. A new roof, small repairs and fresh paint do not call for a new assessment. Before selling, make sure a demolished shed or a finished room is reflected correctly, because a mismatch can turn up during a buyer's title work.

sections.h2: Recording tax when the house sells
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs 50 cents for each $500 of value, and a partial $500 is rounded up, under section 40-22-1. The state treasury receives two-thirds of it and the county treasury one-third. The probate judge works out the tax from the real purchase price, sworn to on a state revenue form, and the probate office tacks on its own recording fee.

When one deed covers land in two or more counties, the state revenue department sets the value for each. Three kinds of deeds escape the tax: corrected deeds, nominal-consideration deeds that perfect a title, and mortgage transfers already taxed.

sections.h2: Selling for cash, with or without repairs
sections.html:
Our offers are for the house in its present condition. Nothing needs fixing first. Send the address and we will walk through your situation, taxes owed included.

  1. Phone the Revenue Commissioner and get the figure due for every tax year.
  2. Find the deed and the newest statement.
  3. Write down repairs, open insurance claims and any tenants.
  4. Compare our offer with your title company's numbers.

Proceeds cover back taxes at closing while the title company files the deed. Cash also means no lender appraisal and no post-inspection repair list, a real plus when a roof, foundation or storm damage would frighten off a financed buyer. Selling a house you inherited? Say so up front so the title company can request probate papers early, and give every heir the same tax figures.

When you accept an offer, the title company or attorney starts a search on the parcel, requests payoffs from the Revenue Commissioner's office and from any lender, and writes up a settlement statement. Review that statement line by line. Taxes, recording costs and any mortgage balance are deducted, and what remains is yours.

Bring photo identification and every key. If the house is in a rural spot with a gate, a well or a shared drive, tell the closing agent so the paperwork describes access correctly. Sellers with a house on acreage should find any survey they have, because a boundary question is easier to settle before the signing than during it.

If you have a homestead or age-based exemption, notify the office after closing. The buyer cannot count on yours and will need to apply separately. Keep your closing papers and the final tax receipt in one place, since you may need them when you file your own income taxes for the year of the sale.

Whether the buyer is an investor, a neighbor or a young family, the first questions are predictable. How old is the roof? Has the house flooded or been hit by a storm? Are the taxes paid up? Which school system serves it? Is the lot on a county road that gets maintained? Answer these before anyone asks and the conversation moves quickly.

For a rental, add the lease terms and the state of the unit. If it is vacant, say how long. Most buyers discount a house that has sat empty, and a clear explanation helps. A cash buyer will still look at everything, but the difference is that the decision does not wait on a bank.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cullman County, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 87,866 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 94,009. That is an increase of 7.0 percent over five years.

faqs.q: Is Cullman County wet or dry?
faqs.a: It is moist. Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville allow alcohol sales, and the rest of the county is dry.

faqs.q: How is a deed taxed in Cullman County?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed, and the probate office collects it when the deed is recorded. Two-thirds goes to the state and one-third to the county.

faqs.q: When do Cullman County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Taxes are due October 1, and unpaid accounts go to the probate court in February with a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cullman County house for cash if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as they stand, so you do not have to fix anything first. Reach out with the address and we will talk through your situation, including any tax owed.
